clue.text: Reduce volume of study, being dim

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
dim and dense both mean slow-witted

explanation.surface: A tired student whose reading pile shrinks because they are too dim to get through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense something is to compress it, so it takes up less space.

clue.text: Arrive at total

definitions.meaning: first meaning: reach, as in coming to a decision
second meaning: amount to, as a bill does

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as reaching a sum, but the two phrases are separate meanings of the same verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to reach a place or conclusion and to add up to a sum.

clue.text: Recently developed shopping centre in Suffolk town

parts.note: something recently developed is new
a market is a place for shopping

explanation.surface: A news item about a fresh shopping development opening in a Suffolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a town in Suffolk, in eastern England, famous for horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the name of a racing town in the English county of Suffolk.

clue.text: Intensely serious boy securing an 'A'

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly, so the boy's name wraps around what follows

parts.note: a boy's name
the letter itself

explanation.surface: A very studious boy who has just secured an A grade.
explanation.walkthrough: The A goes after the first letter of Ernest: E-A-RNEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and grave in manner, fully serious.

clue.text: To avoid committing oneself, suppress article on dealer in stolen goods

parts.note: to sit on a story is to suppress it
the definite article
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods; 'on' places it after the article

explanation.surface: Someone trying to stay neutral while hushing up a story about a receiver of stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay undecided, refusing to take either side in a dispute.

clue.text: Interference in stable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crackling noise on a radio signal

explanation.surface: Someone meddling with horses in a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a building for horses; here it is the adjective meaning unchanging.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for radio crackle and an adjective for something fixed and motionless.

clue.text: Fabric found in Welsh river by Greek character

parts.note: the Taff flows through Cardiff in Wales
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, placed by the river

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth discovered in a Welsh river next to a Greek man.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven silk or synthetic cloth.

clue.text: Trunk and spreading roots

indicators.note: spreading roots move apart and out of place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree described by its trunk and its spreading roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a tree, which the roots reinforce; here it is the body's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs, is the torso.

clue.text: Diffident, girl on the radio in US state capital

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling follows their sound

parts.note: a diffident person is shy
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A timid young woman speaking on the radio in an American state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheyenne is the capital city of Wyoming.

clue.text: Gardening machine male wore out

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who has worn out his lawn machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A mower is a machine for cutting grass in a garden.

clue.text: Time to request church to supply work party

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ask for something is to request it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A call for the church to lay on a working party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is not a celebration but a group of people sent to do a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group assembled to carry out a particular job.

clue.text: So, terse old man battered this creature

indicators.note: something battered is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A curt old man takes a beating from some animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The star-nosed mole is a North American mole with a ring of fleshy tentacles on its snout.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal named is a species of mole, a burrowing mammal.

clue.text: Item used in part payment badly rated at home

indicators.note: badly suggests things done wrong, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: An old appliance valued poorly when offered in part exchange at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-in is an old article handed over to reduce the price of a new one.

clue.text: Captain brought in an eastern plant

indicators.note: something brought in is put inside, so the captain sits within the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A ship's captain hired by an eastern business plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Possibly dig a trench with Ken round vegetable plot

indicators.note: possibly marks the letters as one option among arrangements, so they can be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener named Ken might help dig a trench around the vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen garden is a plot where vegetables and herbs are grown for the household.

clue.text: To con us, concealing annoyance, is risky

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so annoyance goes within

parts.note: to con someone is to do them
anger is strong annoyance

explanation.surface: A warning that cheating us while hiding your irritation is a dangerous game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is slang for swindle, so 'to con us' is DO US, split around ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangerous carries risk of harm, so it is risky.

clue.text: Factory worker and I cover millstone

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker
the pronoun, added on
a cap covers something

explanation.surface: A factory hand and the speaker put a lid on a grinding stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'millstone' suggests grinding mills to fit the factory; it is used figuratively for a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstone round one's neck is a heavy burden, as is a handicap.

clue.text: Following a craze to a certain extent

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: coming after a fad
second meaning: partly, though not very well

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the phrase read word by word: after means following and a fashion is a craze.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in some way but not entirely satisfactorily, so only to some degree.

clue.text: Check about beating

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the pulse is the heart's beating

explanation.surface: Someone checking on a beating heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a test of the pulse, but means stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an attack is to drive it back, to halt or check it.

clue.text: Penetration, in a sense

parts.note: taken as written
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A claim that penetration is true only in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a sense' reads as the qualifying phrase 'sort of'; split, it is IN plus a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is the ability to see deeply into something, a penetrating understanding.

clue.text: Stumped by foreign name for part of a flower

parts.note: st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and altered, so these letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by the foreign name of a botanical part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stumped' looks like 'baffled'; it is the cricket dismissal, written st on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male organ of a flower.

clue.text: Notice father in study, poker-faced

indicators.note: in tells us the first two pieces sit inside the room named next

parts.note: a den is a private study
an ad is a notice or advertisement
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A child notices Dad in his study, wearing an expressionless face.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadpan describes a deliberately expressionless face, like a poker player's.

clue.text: Girl in cream beret

indicators.note: in says the name lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spans the two words

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a cream-coloured beret.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Amber is a female first name, borrowed from the golden fossil resin.

clue.text: Sweet, having hair swept back

indicators.note: swept back, like a hairstyle, runs these letters from right to left

parts.note: tresses are locks of hair

explanation.surface: A cute person with hair brushed backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like 'cute'; in Britain a sweet is a pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a sweet is the dessert course of a meal.

clue.text: Spanish gent in secret plot, with devious role

parts.note: a cabal is a secret plot or the clique behind it

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so these letters go a twisted way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman caught up in a conspiracy, playing a deceitful part.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is Spanish for a gentleman or horseman.

clue.text: Good scope for stable lad

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
room to manoeuvre is scope

explanation.surface: A stable boy is given plenty of opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: A groom looks after horses, the job of a stable lad.

clue.text: Station worker's drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who carries luggage at a railway station

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as possessive, a worker's drink, but stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a luggage carrier at stations and a dark-brown bitter beer.

clue.text: Spray is not working, so discard

parts.note: a jet is a spray of water

indicators.note: working here means being worked over or kneaded, so the preceding letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken spray is useless, so throw it away.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or get rid of something unwanted.
